purpose: Build a positive control for the cell-level nullity branch: generate designs that are expected to do nothing, measure them, and check that the gate fires red on exact equality with the cold no-op reference.

launch_path_defect.finding: This is the only grid in the repository that was not launched through scripts/make_grid_config.py.
launch_path_defect.evidence: .tmp/cfg/grid_nullity_control.json carries acceptance_threshold, re_audit_ratio, purpose and version -- keys the pre-flight never writes -- and points candidates_dir at /workspace/.tmp/cand_nullctl (3 files) instead of the pre-flight's /workspace/.tmp/grid_cand. The other 9 configs in .tmp/cfg/ are exactly the 8-key pre-flight shape.
launch_path_defect.consequence: make_grid_config.py restricts seeds x prompts to the largest rectangle actually present in the candidate pool. On this pool it would have found a 2-cell rectangle, refused the 6-level grid, and exited non-zero. Declaring 3 prompts x 2 seeds against a 3-file pool instead let the harness fill the missing cells itself.

harness_substitution.mechanism: generate_candidate() used `pool = matching or candidates`: when no candidate carried the requested (generator_seed, prompt) pair it selected one from the whole pool by a hash of the prompt, then setdefault-stamped the missing labels onto it and recomputed candidate_sha256. The stamped labels are the candidate's own, so the raw evidence stays internally consistent and only the design identity is false.
harness_substitution.fix: chia_loop/loops/audit_repro.py now raises ValueError listing the levels the pool actually offers; chia_loop/tests/test_audit_repro.py::test_missing_cell_is_refused_instead_of_substituted locks it; scripts/audit_grid_levels.py gates published grids on three witnesses (generator_seed vs cell seed, pool membership where recorded, and design_sha256 distinctness per level).
harness_substitution.independent_confirmation: scripts/check_grid_evidence.py reaches the same conclusion from binary digests alone: one_design_per_binary fails with binary 3189efdc1e54e5b5 recorded for 4 design labels, and it reports 3 distinct binaries for 6 designs. It never reads the labels, so the two methods do not share a failure mode.

discarded.unit_note: Both values are fractions, not percentages: 0.083812 = 8.38% against a 5% gate, 0.116232 = 11.62%. Sibling artifacts in this repository record the same statistic as *_cv_pct.
discarded.reason: Every factor axis of this grid is uninterpretable, and each axis carries both error types. The only nonzero cross-seed CV (0.083812 on ligra_BFSCC, under prompt=fill_only_conservative) compares two different compiled designs, design_sha256 50378a32b274 (gen_fill_only_conservative_s0) and ee6081546365 (gen_default_s0, sitting at a substituted level), so it is a design difference mislabelled as a seed effect, and it is what drove the BLOCKED verdict. The 0.0 CVs are not one error but two. Under prompt=default both levels resolve to one design (ee6081546365), so its 0.0 is the same binary measured twice -- a manufactured pass. Under prompt=aggressive_offset the two levels are genuinely distinct designs (ee6081546365 and 265e87b8b3bd) whose cycles coincide because both are inert against the cold no-op reference on all three traces; that equality is real and is kept below as absolute equality, but the coincidence is arranged by the substitution -- which design sat at aggressive_offset/0 was chosen by the bug, not by the design -- so the axis still cannot be quoted as a reproducibility measurement. All three prompt axes contain at least one substituted level (aggressive_offset/0, default/1, fill_only_conservative/1), so no threshold decision from this grid can be quoted; what survives is absolute equality against the reference and within-cell repeat determinism.
discarded.also_discarded: n_designs_null_on_every_trace = 5 from check_grid_evidence.py: four of those five labels are the same design counted once per name. The true count is 2.

reason_correction_2026_09_25.printed_before: Every variance axis of this grid is uninterpretable, in both directions. The nonzero cross-seed CV appears only under prompt=fill_only_conservative, whose two 'seeds' are two different designs (c57d6ee71b1a and 332147378a88), so it is a design difference mislabelled as a seed effect -- and it is what drove the BLOCKED verdict. The 0.0 CVs on the other levels are the opposite error: the same binary measured twice, which is a manufactured pass. One bug therefore supplied both the false alarm and the false reassurance, so no threshold decision from this grid can be quoted.
reason_correction_2026_09_25.what_was_wrong: (1) It quoted c57d6ee71b1a and 332147378a88 as the two designs, but those are candidate_sha256 values, which cover the candidate's own labels and so are not design identities; the design digests are 50378a32b274 and ee6081546365. The same file's harness_substitution.substituted_onto already keeps the two kinds apart. (2) It asserted that every 0.0 CV on the other levels was one binary measured twice. That holds for prompt=default only; prompt=aggressive_offset spans two distinct designs that are both inert, and calling that a double measurement contradicts the positive-control passage in paper/paper.tex, which names exactly those two designs. (3) It gave max_seed_cv and max_prompt_spread with no unit.
reason_correction_2026_09_25.what_did_not_change: The disposition. Each prompt axis still contains at least one substituted level, the verdict stays NON-REPRODUCIBLE, the publish gate stays BLOCKED, and no threshold decision from this grid is quotable. The correction changes the account of why, not what is discarded.
reason_correction_2026_09_25.evidence: per-axis values in results/grid_nullity_control/audit_report.json (seed_cv per prompt and trace); design_sha256 per cell in results/grid_nullity_control/raw.json; reproduced by python3 scripts/audit_grid_levels.py

positive_control.claim: Two delivered designs are bit-identical to the cold no-op reference on every trace they were measured on, which is the exact-equality condition the null_on_every_measured_trace branch is written to reject. Before this grid that branch had only a synthetic control.
positive_control.note: Neither binary equals the image default binary 688278205d6c9fa4, so these are compiled, delivered modules that change nothing measurable -- not a build that silently fell back to the default.

negative_control.note: Live on all three traces, and faster than the no-op on all three: the only design in this grid that measurably does something removes work rather than adding it.

repeat_determinism.why_it_survives: Repeated-run CV compares trials inside one cell, so it never touches a factor label. Two trials of each of the 3 real designs on each trace agreed exactly.

kept.ranking_tie: The two null designs share mean cycles 3668738.666667 across the three traces and rank below gen_fill_only_conservative_s0 at 3376448.666667, i.e. the ranking agrees with the nullity finding rather than with the labels.

clean_grids.claim: Defect 8 is confined to this grid. Every other published grid carries one distinct compiled design per factor level and no label disagreement.
clean_grids.stub_backend: The stub fixture had the same class of problem for a different reason: its 4-entry catalog carried no generator_seed or prompt at all, so all 9 of its levels were stamped rather than matched. Its design pool is a fixture (cycles come from StubBackend arithmetic), so this was invisible to the label witnesses and only the digest witness found it. The catalog now enumerates all 9 labelled cells explicitly.
